records.label: spacr.channel_sorting#3
records.source: 1. **Channels and sets.** Each image gets a CHANNEL, and images that show the same field in different channels share a SET. Channels come from the user's selection (:func:`parse_names` ``channels=``) or from a regex's ``chanID`` group; sets come from the regex's other named groups (:func:`parse_names`, checked by :func:`check_sets`), from a regex spaCR proposes (:func:`infer_regex`), or, ignoring names, from pairing each image with the most similar image of the same size in every other channel (:func:`detect_sets`). 2. **The plan.** :func:`build_plan` names every set in the Yokogawa / CellVoyager form ``plate1_A01_T0001F001L01A01Z01C01.tif`` -- exactly what ``spacr.utils._get_regex('cellvoyager', ...)`` parses -- and lists every move. It writes nothing. 3. **Apply.** :func:`apply_plan` moves each image into ``C01/``, ``C02/``... under a new folder, its mask into that channel folder's ``masks/`` under the new name (and its ``.curation.json`` ledger with it, so the pairing survives), records every move in ``channel_sorting_manifest.csv``, and then :func:`merge_sorted` builds ``stack/``, ``masks/<role>_mask_stack/`` and ``merged/`` with spaCR's own functions (:func:`spacr.utils._extract_filename_metadata`, :func:`spacr.io._escaped_field_stem` and :func:`spacr.io._load_and_concatenate_arrays`), so each merged array has the pipeline's own layout: intensity channels first, then one label plane per mask role in the order cell, nucleus, pathogen.
records.context: 1. **Image data channels and sets.** Each image gets an image data channel, and images that show the same microscope field of view in different image data channels share a SET. image data channels come from the user's selection (:func:`parse_names` ``channels=``) or from a regex's ``chanID`` group; sets come from the regex's other named groups (:func:`parse_names`, checked by :func:`check_sets`), from a regex spaCR proposes (:func:`infer_regex`), or, ignoring names, from pairing each image with the most similar image of the same size in every other image data channel (:func:`detect_sets`). 2. **The plan.** :func:`build_plan` names every set in the Yokogawa / CellVoyager form ``plate1_A01_T0001F001L01A01Z01C01.tif`` -- exactly what ``spacr.utils._get_regex('cellvoyager', ...)`` parses -- and lists every move. It writes nothing. 3. **Apply.** :func:`apply_plan` moves each image into ``C01/``, ``C02/``... under a new folder, its mask into that image data channel folder's ``masks/`` under the new name (and its ``.curation.json`` ledger with it, so the pairing survives), records every move in ``channel_sorting_manifest.csv``, and then :func:`merge_sorted` builds ``stack/``, ``masks/<role>_mask_stack/`` and ``merged/`` with spaCR's own functions (:func:`spacr.utils._extract_filename_metadata`, :func:`spacr.io._escaped_field_stem` and :func:`spacr.io._load_and_concatenate_arrays`), so each merged array has the workflow's own layout: intensity image data channels first, then one label image layer per mask role in the order cell, nucleus, pathogen.
records.translation: 1. **Canales y conjuntos.** Cada imagen recibe un CANAL, y las imágenes que muestran el mismo campo de visión en canales distintos comparten un CONJUNTO. Los canales proceden de la selección del usuario (:func:`parse_names` ``channels=``) o del grupo ``chanID`` de una expresión regular; los conjuntos proceden de los demás grupos con nombre de la expresión regular (:func:`parse_names`, comprobados por :func:`check_sets`), de una expresión regular que propone spaCR (:func:`infer_regex`) o, sin tener en cuenta los nombres, de emparejar cada imagen con la imagen más parecida del mismo tamaño en cada uno de los demás canales (:func:`detect_sets`). 2. **El plan.** :func:`build_plan` nombra cada conjunto con la forma Yokogawa / CellVoyager ``plate1_A01_T0001F001L01A01Z01C01.tif`` -- exactamente lo que analiza ``spacr.utils._get_regex('cellvoyager', ...)`` -- y enumera cada movimiento. No escribe nada. 3. **Aplicar.** :func:`apply_plan` mueve cada imagen a ``C01/``, ``C02/``... bajo una carpeta nueva, su máscara al ``masks/`` de esa carpeta de canal con el nombre nuevo (y su registro ``.curation.json`` con ella, para que el emparejamiento se conserve), anota cada movimiento en ``channel_sorting_manifest.csv`` y después :func:`merge_sorted` construye ``stack/``, ``masks/<role>_mask_stack/`` y ``merged/`` con las funciones propias de spaCR (:func:`spacr.utils._extract_filename_metadata`, :func:`spacr.io._escaped_field_stem` y :func:`spacr.io._load_and_concatenate_arrays`), de modo que cada matriz fusionada tiene la estructura propia de la pipeline: primero los canales de intensidad y después un plano de etiquetas por papel de máscara en el orden célula, núcleo, patógeno.

records.source: Regex conventions: ``chanID`` is the channel; ``plateID``, ``wellID``, ``fieldID`` and ``timeID`` say where a set goes; any other named group only helps tell sets apart. A group that did not take part in a match counts as the empty string, so an optional ``(?:_(?P<fieldID>\d+))?`` reads the numbered copies :mod:`spacr.folder_consolidation` makes.
records.context: Regex conventions: ``chanID`` is the channel; ``plateID``, ``wellID``, ``fieldID`` and ``timeID`` say where a set goes; any other named group only helps tell sets apart. A group that did not take part in a match counts as the empty string, so an optional ``(?:_(?P<fieldID>\d+))?`` reads the numbered copies :mod:`spacr.folder_consolidation` makes.
records.translation: Convenciones de expresiones regulares: ``chanID`` es el canal; ``plateID``, ``wellID``, ``fieldID`` y ``timeID`` indican adónde va un conjunto; cualquier otro grupo con nombre solo ayuda a distinguir conjuntos. Un grupo que no participó en una coincidencia cuenta como la cadena vacía, así que un ``(?:_(?P<fieldID>\d+))?`` opcional lee las copias numeradas que crea :mod:`spacr.folder_consolidation`.

records.context: Self-supervised denoising comes before the chain. With ``n2v_denoise`` on, a Noise2Void (N2V2) model per segmentation image data channel is trained by CAREamics, in its own environment, on a sample of the processing session's own raw microscope fields of view -- no clean images are needed -- or read from ``n2v_model``. Each microscope field of view's selected image data channels are denoised after illumination correction and before the PSF and the chain, while the noise is still independent from pixel to pixel, which is what Noise2Void assumes. The checkpoints' hashes and the training record join the same provenance record.
records.translation: LA ELIMINACIÓN DE RUIDO AUTOSUPERVISADA VA ANTES DE LA CADENA. Con ``n2v_denoise`` activado, CAREamics entrena un modelo Noise2Void (N2V2) por canal de segmentación, en su propio entorno, con una muestra de los campos de visión en bruto de la propia ejecución -- no hacen falta imágenes limpias --, o lo lee de ``n2v_model``.
